$comment: The settings every plugin dialog is built from (plugins/shared/README.md).

key: an option of fins_entry.js computeFins, dotted for a nested one (sway.on -> {sway: {on}}). Hosts never assemble that object themselves: pass the dialog's {key: value} -- in the ENTRY's units, so a percent control's value / 100 -- to optionsFromDialog() (fins_entry.js; Python: supportfins_host.host_options), which nests, checks and drops sway when it is off. It refuses a value out of range rather than guess; null or '' means the default.

default/min/max/step: in the ENTRY's units. percent: true = show value x 100 (the site's sliders read 0-100) and round to step for display. slider: a range control rather than a number field. hint: the site's muted text after the label (units live here).

showIf: the control is shown only when EVERY item holds; an item is a bool key (on), {key, in: [values]}, or {any: [items]}. Evaluate with optionVisible() (fins_entry.js); hidden values may still be sent, the engine ignores them.

hostSupplied: 'slicer' = a slicer plugin reads this from the slicer's own settings and leaves it out of its dialog; CAD hosts show it. Its range is the dialog's, not a limit: the host's own value is used as is. threshold is NOT a slicer's support angle: it is measured from the plate, where Cura's is from vertical.

site: the matching control id in web/index.html; plugins/shared/tests/options.test.js pins defaults, ranges and choices to it, and lists every site control this file leaves out on purpose (placement mode: plugins run Auto; Custom pad and Support gap: hand-typed numbers, the material sets the clearances).

options.label: Material
options.tooltip: The filament you'll print in. PETG fuses to supports much harder than PLA, so PETG loosens the gaps and gives the bed pad a gap instead of a tack. PLA keeps the tighter grip.

options.label: Overhang
options.tooltip: Surface angle from the plate below which a face needs support.

options.label: Tines
options.tooltip: Tines fuse the support to the part so it grips instead of just propping. Off = plain breakaway wall.

options.label: Tine grip
options.tooltip: How tightly to space the grip tines. Light = fewest marks (default), a per-wall floor keeps grip; Firm = dense comb / max grip for a tippy or tall part.

options.label: Layer height
options.tooltip: Set this to the layer height you slice at. The grip tines are one layer tall so they snap off clean; if this doesn't match your slicer, the tines tear and leave marks. Default 0.2mm.

options.label: Bed pad
options.tooltip: A tilted part rests on an edge and peels off the plate without a pad. Auto: Light, or Sure hold when the part meets the plate on a point or a small round foot. Light: one layer, 0.12mm off the part, peels off like a brim. Sure hold: thicker and tacked into the part, holds harder but is harder to remove.

options.label: Sway braces
options.tooltip: Stand tapered buttress ribs against the upright sides of a tall part, tied on with tines all the way up, so it doesn't drift or wobble as it grows.

options.label: Brace grip from
options.tooltip: Height the brace tines start at. 0 = grip the whole height; raise it to tie on only above where the part starts to move.

options.label: Brace tine spacing
options.tooltip: Vertical distance between brace tines. Smaller = held tighter, more marks on the side. Default 6mm.

options.label: Brace depth
options.tooltip: How far the brace reaches out at the bed, as a share of its height. Deeper = stiffer, more plastic. Default 15%.

options.label: Cutouts
options.tooltip: Cut holes through tall breakaway walls to save filament. The top edge that holds the part, the foot, and the wall's ends stay solid, and every hole has a pointed roof so it prints without bridging. Short walls stay solid.

options.label: Wide-face coverage
options.tooltip: How densely to line a WIDE overhang face with fins. The middle is the anti-sag default; drag LEFT for fewer fins (a small part can go down to one — the readout warns if a broad face then risks sagging), RIGHT for more support. Narrow parts are unaffected.

options.label: Plate only
options.tooltip: Stand every support on the build plate, never on the part itself. An overhang with part under it is left unsupported, and the readout says how many.
